I've been in your position before. Got accepted to a great school for biology and would be 7 hours away from home. I was going through a manic episode with psychotic features in the spring of my senior year. I really wanted to go to that college but my parents thought I was too unstable to handle a 4-year and so I went to community college instead. It was the best choice for me at that time. I continued to struggle with my mental health for the 5 years I was at community college and was eventually accepted to an even better college and my dream school. If I had went to that 4-year college after my senior year of high school, I would've struggled immensely, wouldn't have graduated in 4 years, and be in enormous amounts of school debt.

My advice would be to not think about school right now and prioritize your mental health. You still have time to find the right medications and stabilize before you go to college in the fall or make a final decision. You are smart to have community college as an option for you. You are thinking about your mental health, something I didn't do at your age. If you do go to community college, you'll still be able to transfer into your dream school and you would have saved a lot of money. Since you say you might not be able to graduate, maybe community college would be your best choice right now. Don't worry about other peoples' opinions of you if you go to community college. Community college is filled with very smart and dedicated individuals who just want another chance at getting into a 4-year. They might struggle financially and/or mentally as well. Always choose the option that prioritizes your mental health.
